answer: Randomized quorum assignment. Each epoch, a public verifiable random function draws identity-to-task assignments from a river of candidates, so an attacker cannot predict which agents will review or countersign a given action. To hold N identities, the attacker must actually operate each one through unpredictable shifts, paying real compute and infrastructure per identity; idle sybils fall out of the lagoon of eligible signers and lose standing. A per-epoch presence check keyed to the draw (a quartz nonce signed within the assigned window) enforces liveness.
